Ciosure:  Various closure modalities were discussed with the patient, and it was decided that a complex linear repair would best preserve normal anatomic and functional relationships. Due to the size and location of the defect, and the need to achieve optimal functionality, cosmesis, avoid hematoma, and prevent wound dehiscence, it was decided that a complex linear closure would provide the best match. Additional risk of wound dehiscence was discussed.  The patient was placed on the operating room table. The area was anesthetized with Lidocaine 1% with epinephrine with added sodium bicarbonate, was given a sterile prep using chlorhexidine, and draped in the usual sterile fashion. Recreation and enlargement of the wound was performed by excising cones of tissue via the triangulation technique.  The final incision lines were placed with respect for the patient's natural skin tension lines in a linear configuration to avoid functional and aesthetic distortion of adjacent free margins. Following extensive undermining, meticulous hemostasis was obtained with spot pressure. Subcutaneous dead space, dermis, and epidermis were closed with 5-0 Monocryl using dermal vertical mattress stitches and 5-0 Prolene. Final closure length: 4.5cm. The following is a clinical rationale CVS Caremark used to make our decision:  RATIONALE The intent of the criteria is to ensure that patients follow selection elements noted in labeling and/or practice guidelines in order to decrease the potential for inappropriate utilization and misuse of medications.  The intent of this program is to confirm the medical necessity of formulary medication quantity limits exceeding the initial limit, or to confirm the appropriate coverage of a non-formulary prescription medication for patients. These criteria apply to all medications listed in the table above.  This policy is intended to ensure that medications above subject to exception prior authorization by the Plan are utilized in accordance with FDA indications and uses found in the compendia of current literature including American Hospital Formulary Service Drug Information (AHFS), Micromedex, or current accepted guidelines. This policy also aims to ensure that medications are approved within manufacturer's dosing guidelines or dosing guidelines of current compendia and to foster cost-effective, first-line use of available formulary/preferred drug list medications.  If the prescriber provides evidence, such as chart notes, of trial and failure of 3 formulary alternatives (generics and/or formulary brands) in a class with 3 or more alternatives available, the prior authorization will be approved. If the prescriber provides evidence, such as chart notes, of trial and failure of 2 formulary alternatives (generics and/or formulary brands) in a class with 2 alternatives available, the prior authorization will be approved. If the prescriber provides evidence, such as chart notes, of trial and failure of 1 formulary alternative (generic and/or formulary brands) in a class where only one alternative exists, the prior authorization will be approved.  lf the request is for a non-formulary combination product for which individual components are available at similar doses on formulary, then the separate individual components of the combination product taken concurrently must be unable to be taken PLUS the remaining required number of alternatives, and the patient must have had a trial and failure of the separate individual components due to an adverse event (examples: rash, nausea, vomiting, anaphylaxis) that is thought to be due to an inactive ingredient. Chart documentation or MedWatch form of the adverse event must be provided, documenting date/time, and severity of the adverse event, dosage and duration of medication treatment, interventions and relevant tests or laboratory data.  \f their request is for a non-formulary brand name product that has a generic available on formulary, then the formulary generic must be unable to be taken PLUS the remaining required number of alternatives, and the patient must have had a trial and failure of the generic agent due to an adverse event (examples: rash, nausea, vomiting, anaphylaxis) that is thought to be due to an inactive ingredient. Chart documentation or MedWatch form of the reaction must be provided, documenting date/time, and severity of the adverse event, dosage and duration of medication treatment, interventions and relevant tests or laboratory data.  If the request is for a non-formulary product with an available alternative dosage form for the same active ingredient on formulary, then an alternative formulary dosage form of the requested drug must be unable to be taken PLUS the remaining required number of formulary alternatives, and there must be a clinical reason why the patient is unable to take an applicable alternative formulary dosage form based on the patient's condition (e.g. age, indication).  If the prescriber provides evidence, such as chart notes, of a clinical condition or need for a specific dosage form for which there is no formulary alternative or if the listed formulary alternatives are not recommended based on published guidelines or clinical literature OR the formulary alternatives will likely be ineffective or less effective for the patient OR the formulary alternatives will likely cause an adverse effect, the claim should be approved. This includes if the request is for diabetic supply/insulin cartridge and visual impairment is noted, or if the request is for non-formulary test strips and the patient is on an insulin pump that requires the requested test strips.

Universal statin therapy for diabetics: Recommend statin therapy (such as atorvastatin or rosuvastatin) for all diabetic patients ages 40 to 75 without considering their LDL levels.  Customized treatment intensity: Select moderate or high-intensity statins based on the presence of additional cardiovascular risk factors. To combat this, national guidelines advocate for statin therapy for all diabetic patients ages 40 to 75, irrespective of LDL cholesterol levels, to prevent cardiovascular diseases.  * Proven benefits: - Statins can lower LDL-C levels by approximately 39 mg/dL: - This reduction translates to a 13% decrease in heart disease and stroke mortality, regardless of baseline LDL levels.' *« Current gaps in statin use: - Nearly 60% of eligible patients are not offered statin therapy by their healthcare provider. - Only 50% of adults in the United States who benefit from statins are currently taking them - Primary non-adherence is a challenge, with 34% of patients not filling their initial statin prescription*  Understanding the SUPD quality measure The Statin Use in Patients with Diabetes (SUPD) measure is recognized as a quality Star measure by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS). * Measure definition: - Targets Medicare Part D beneficiaries ages 40 to 75 with diabetes - Includes those who received at least two diabetes medication fills and a statin during the measurement period  Enhancing statin adherence: best practices To improve adherence and health outcomes, consider these strategies:  Anta 3.e Coss ave Bue Sho is tle bade amet hi Colores: Rolly Mour.ur osviluand Medel Sevig ho YO recus wea Le iby IMS Coney be Carre Aer Heo lt Pars bel Seo-cir Elue Cross Bue Sve eu rure 2a Geog’, In. 1 eine: Aalber reo Corporres, 1c Ir Realky Ailend eulh Pare of ertucey be ine Athen Heol Parscfltate, Ire 1 V’sscuni (exduo"y 2S contest ne Caren Ty oven): ROPICHOKE® Vacaced fare, ie. Universal statin therapy for diabetics: Recommend statin therapy (such as atorvastatin or rosuvastatin) for all diabetic patients ages 40 to 75 without considering their LDL levels.  Customized treatment intensity: Select moderate or high-intensity statins based on the presence of additional cardiovascular risk factors.  Education, engagement, and monitoring: Engage patients in understanding statins, dispel misconceptions about side effects, ensure adherence through regular follow-ups, and manage muscle-related side effects effectively.  Help patients achieve cardiovascular health milestones Care providers can significantly reduce cardiovascular risks among diabetic patients and improve overall outcomes. The following is a clinical rationale CVS Caremark used to make our decision:  RATIONALE The intent of the criteria is to ensure that patients follow selection elements noted in labeling and/or practice guidelines in order to decrease the potential for inappropriate utilization and misuse of medications.  The intent of this program is to confirm the medical necessity of formulary medication quantity limits exceeding the initial limit, or to confirm the appropriate coverage of a non-formulary prescription medication for patients. These criteria apply to all medications listed in the table above.  This policy is intended to ensure that medications above subject to exception prior authorization by the Plan are utilized in accordance with FDA indications and uses found i in the compendia of current literature including American Hcepita!  guidelines. This policy also aims to ensure that medications z are approved within manufacturer's dosing guidelines or dosing guidelines of current compendia and to foster cost-effective, first-line use of available formulary/preferred drug list medications.  If the prescriber provides evidence, such as chart notes, of trial and failure of 3 formulary alternatives (generics and/or formulary brands) in a class with 3 or more alternatives available, the prior authorization will be approved. If the prescriber provides evidence, such as chart notes, of trial and failure of 2 formulary alternatives (generics and/or formulary brands) in a class with 2 alternatives available, the prior authorization will be approved. If the prescriber provides evidence, such as chart notes, of trial and failure of 1 formulary alternative (generic and/or formulary brands) in a class where only one alternative exists, the prior authorization will be approved.  lf the request is for a non-formulary combination product for which individual components are available at similar doses on formulary, then the separate individual components of the combination product taken concurrently must be unable to be taken PLUS the remaining required number of alternatives, and the patient must have had a trial and failure of the separate individual components due to an adverse event (examples: rash, nausea, vomiting, anaphylaxis) that is thought to be due to an inactive ingredient. Chart documentation or MedWatch form of the adverse event must be provided, documenting date/time, and severity of the adverse event, dosage and duration of medication treatment, interventions and relevant tests or laboratory data.  \f their request is for a non-formulary brand name product that has a generic available on formulary, then the formulary generic must be unable to be taken PLUS the remaining required number of alternatives, and the patient must have had a trial and failure of the generic agent due to an adverse event (examples: rash, nausea, vomiting, anaphylaxis) that is thought to be due to an inactive ingredient. Chart documentation or MedWatch form of the reaction must be provided, documenting date/time, and severity of the adverse event, dosage and duration of medication treatment, interventions and relevant tests or laboratory data.  If the request is for a non-formulary product with an available alternative dosage form for the same active ingredient on formulary, then an alternative formulary dosage form of the requested drug must be unable to be taken PLUS the remaining required number of formulary alternatives, and there must be a clinical reason why the patient is unable to take an applicable alternative formulary dosage form based on the patient's condition (e.g. age, indication).  If the prescriber provides evidence, such as chart notes, of a clinical condition or need for a specific dosage form for which there is no formulary alternative or if the listed formulary alternatives are not recommended based on published guidelines or clinical literature OR the formulary alternatives will likely be ineffective or less effective for the patient OR the formulary alternatives will likely cause an adverse effect, the claim should be approved. HELPFUL HINTS FOR COMPLETING THE EXTERNAL APPEAL APPLICATION Some sections of the application can be confusing. This will help explain what is expected for those sections. Application  e Number 11 is only required if the patient has designated someone other than the provider to act on their behalf.  e Number 12 indicates the reason the health plan denied the service. This information is found on the Final Adverse Determination (denial letter) from the health plan.  e The Type of Review must be completed in number 13 if an expedited appeal is being requested.  External Appeals can only be expedited if the denial falls into one of these categories. If you already received the services, your appeal cannot be expedited. You must also indicate if this is for a Standard Formulary Exception or a Standard External Appeal.  e Number 14 is required if the provider is submitting the application on their own behalf or behalf of the patient.  e Number 45 is to be used to describe the services requested. You can attach a separate document with this information.  e Number 17 relates to the fee that a health plan may charge for the external appeal. The final adverse determination will indicate if the health plan charges a fee.  e Patient Consent to the Release of Records for NYS External Appeal -this document must be signed by the patient or their authorized representative. If the patient is a minor, the document must be signed by their parent or legal guardian. If the patient is deceased, the document must be signed by the patient's healthcare proxy or executor. If signed by a guardian, healthcare proxy or executor, a copy of the legal supporting document should be included.  Physician's Attestation  e For medical necessity, experimental/investigational, and out-of-network appeals, the first section is required if the attending physician is requesting an expedited appeal because the standard 30-day timeframe would jeopardize the patient's life, health or ability to regain maximum function, or the delay would pose an imminent or serious threat to the patient's health. The attending physician must also include a phone number where they can be reached during non-business hours. This is important since the External Appeal Agent must make a determination within 72 hours of receipt. The decision must be issued even in the event of incomplete medical information or unanswered questions due to the inability to reach the attending physician.  e For formulary exception appeals, the first section is required if the attending physician or prescriber is requesting an expedited appeal because the patient is suffering from a health condition that may seriously jeopardize his or her life, health, or ability to regain maximum function, or is undergoing a current course of treatment using a non-formulary drug.
